title: INTELLECTUAL DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER WITH POOR GROWTH AND WITH OR WITHOUT SEIZURES OR ATAXIA

relationships.phenotype: INTELLECTUAL DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER WITH POOR GROWTH AND WITH OR WITHOUT SEIZURES OR ATAXIA

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that intellectual developmental disorder with poor growth and with or without seizures or ataxia (IDPOGSA) is caused by recessively inherited mutation in the ABCA2 gene (600047) on chromosome 9q34.3.

checks.claim: Intellectual developmental disorder with poor growth and with or without seizures or ataxia (IDPOGSA) is caused by recessively inherited mutation in the ABCA2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Although recessively inherited ABCA2 variants have been reported in two patients who had intellectual disability with global developmental delays, our study demonstrates the role of an ABCA2 variant in the pathogenesis of ataxia with dysarthria.
checks.explanation: The abstract links recessive ABCA2 variants to intellectual disability and links an ABCA2 frameshift in a consanguineous family to ataxia with dysarthria. It does not mention the combined IDPOGSA entity, poor growth or seizures. It also never states that this family's variant is homozygous or recessively inherited.

checks.claim: The ABCA2 gene is located on chromosome 9q34.3.
checks.evidence_quote: Whole-exome sequencing data analyses identified a frameshift variant, c.4993delG:p.(Val1665TyrfsTer36) in ABCA2 (NM_212533.2)
checks.explanation: The abstract does not give the chromosomal location. The draft adds 9q34.3 as standard nomenclature for the ABCA2 gene the paper names, which the instructions count as supported.

paragraphs.text: Aslam and Naz (2019) studied a consanguineous Pakistani family with a movement disorder affecting 2 sibs. Both affected individuals had symptoms consistent with cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria. Brain MRI showed no abnormalities. Both affected individuals had elevated low density lipoprotein levels in their blood. The authors described their report as an extension of the phenotypic spectrum associated with ABCA2.

checks.claim: Aslam and Naz (2019) studied a consanguineous Pakistani family in which 2 sibs were affected by a movement disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: The study was conducted to identify the molecular basis of a movement disorder in a consanguineous Pakistani family.
checks.explanation: The methods also refer to 'two siblings affected with a movement disorder'.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern in the consanguineous Pakistani family reported by Aslam and Naz (2019) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.explanation: The family is consanguineous and the abstract cites recessive ABCA2 variants, but it never states that this family's inheritance pattern is autosomal recessive.

paragraphs.text: In 2 sibs from a consanguineous Pakistani family with cerebellar ataxia and dysarthria, Aslam and Naz (2019) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a frameshift mutation in the ABCA2 gene (c.4993delG; Val1665TyrfsTer36; NM_212533.2). Sanger sequencing showed that the mutation segregated with the disorder in the family. It was absent from all publicly available databases and from ethnically matched controls.

paragraphs.text: In 2 sibs from a consanguineous Pakistani family with cerebellar ataxia, dysarthria and elevated low density lipoprotein levels, Aslam and Naz (2019) identified a 1-bp deletion in the ABCA2 gene (c.4993delG, NM_212533.2). The deletion causes a frameshift and a premature termination codon (Val1665TyrfsTer36). Whole-exome sequencing identified the mutation, and Sanger sequencing showed that it segregated with the disorder in the family. It was absent from all publicly available databases and from ethnically matched controls.

checks.claim: Aslam and Naz (2019) identified a 1-bp deletion in the ABCA2 gene (c.4993delG, NM_212533.2) in 2 sibs from a consanguineous Pakistani family with cerebellar ataxia, dysarthria, and elevated low density lipoprotein levels.
checks.evidence_quote: Whole-exome sequencing data analyses identified a frameshift variant, c.4993delG:p.(Val1665TyrfsTer36) in ABCA2 (NM_212533.2)
checks.explanation: Variant, transcript, family and phenotype match. The abstract calls it a frameshift variant and gives the c.4993delG notation, but does not use the words '1-bp deletion'.

checks.claim: The ABCA2 c.4993delG deletion causes a frameshift and a premature termination codon (Val1665TyrfsTer36).
checks.evidence_quote: a frameshift variant, c.4993delG:p.(Val1665TyrfsTer36)
checks.explanation: The 'fsTer36' notation means a frameshift ending in a premature stop codon.
